entries.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
techniqueCitations: Video: Dumbbell Floor Press technique demonstration (YouTube, video ID VmB1G1K7v94).
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository as the horizontal-press (supine) family base: lying on the back with the knees bent and feet planted, the spine exactly 24 units and the neck exactly 9, and the floor press arm path running from straight over the chest to the soft floor touch beside the chest. Draft preview pending qualified technique review. Card tightened from 76 x 46 to 64 x 36: the joints span x 22.0..72.5 and y 68.5..95.0, so the old card carried about ten units of dead margin on every side and the athlete read small. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a dumbbell floor press, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Start with the dumbbells over the chest, elbows about 45 degrees.
Lower with the wrists stacked over the elbows.
Touch down soft; let the upper arms meet the floor.
Pause on the floor.
Drive back up through the same line.
Finish over the chest with straight arms.

entries.name: Close-Grip Dumbbell Press
techniqueCitations: Video: Close-Grip Dumbbell Press technique demonstration (YouTube, video ID lNPH4gf4g08).
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: on the flat bench (the supine precedent body, spine exactly 24 and neck exactly 9), the two bells are pressed together over the mid-chest and drawn as one compact pair with a tighter far-limb offset, so the close grip reads closer than the floor press; the elbows stay tucked to the ribs through the press. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a close-grip dumbbell press, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Start with the bells pressed together over the middle of the chest.
Keep crushing; lower the pair toward the chest.
Elbows close to the ribs; touch softly.
Stay crushed and pause at the chest.
Press the pair back up as one unit.
Finish stacked, still crushing the bells.

entries.name: Alternating Floor Press
entries.reason: Own drawn frames for the family base, and the alternation is now actually visible: the working bell travels while the other waits at the lockout, with the roles swapping at the hand-off, so the two no longer draw on top of each other. Card tightened from 76 x 46 to 64 x 36 around the figure, which had been sitting small in a card with about ten units of dead margin on every side. The elbow is solved on the shoulder circle from the authored hand, so the upper arm (12.5) and forearm (12.0) hold their length by construction. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Nine drawn positions of an alternating kettlebell floor press, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Near bell at the lockout, far bell waiting above the chest.
The near bell starts down; the far bell stays parked.
Near bell touches the floor.
Swap: the far bell takes over from here.
Far bell at the lockout, near bell waiting above the chest.
The far bell starts down; the near bell stays parked.
Far bell touches the floor.
Press back up through the same path.
Both bells finish together at the lockout.

entries.name: Barbell Bench Press - Medium Grip
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: on the flat bench (the supine precedent body, spine exactly 24 and neck exactly 9), the bar rides the elbow-stacked press line and is drawn end-on with its plates by the perspective-barbell machinery from the b joint at the near grip. No database media row exists under this name; the standard bench setup was drawn (listed in the daily review; the rack uprights are not drawn, the cue shows the bar and plates). Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Eight drawn positions of a barbell bench press, medium grip, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Start with the bar over the chest and the wrists stacked over the elbows.
Lower to the chest along the same line.
Keep the elbows under the bar as the bar descends.
Bar at the chest; keep the shoulder blades set.
Pause at the chest.
Drive through the bar; keep the path the same.
Keep pressing straight through the same line.
Finish over the chest with straight arms.

entries.name: Bench Press - With Bands
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, from the description accepted that day: the earlier drawing showed a barbell with a band over it, where the text has no barbell: a band with a handle in each hand. Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 30 degrees so both arms and both strands of the band show: lying on a flat bench with the feet on the floor, a band from under the bench's head-end leg to a handle in each hand; the arms start straight above the chest with the hands shoulder-width apart, lower slowly until the elbows are at right angles with the upper arms about forty-five degrees out from the sides, and press back to straight for a one-second squeeze. Lowering takes more than twice as long as pressing. The band only lengthens on the press. Not drawn: which way the palms face.
entries.summary: Lying on a flat bench with a band trapped under its head-end leg and a handle in each hand, lower slowly until the elbows are at ninety degrees, press back to straight arms and squeeze for a second.

frames.caption: Trap the middle of a band with handles under the head-end leg of a flat bench, checking it cannot slip, then take a handle in each hand and lie back with the arms straight above the chest, hands shoulder-width apart and palms facing your feet.
Lower the handles slowly until the elbows are bent to ninety degrees.
Shoulder blades set on the bench. Elbows to ninety degrees.
Press back up to straight arms.
Squeeze the chest for a second. Twice as long down as up.

entries.name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Press
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: on the flat bench with the elbows anchored tight to the ribs - the close grip as it reads in a side view - and the bar drawn end-on with its plates from the b joint. In a pure side view the hand-to-hand width is invisible, so the close grip reads through the tucked elbows and the captions; listed in the daily review. The EZ-bar is drawn in the standard straight bar form. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Eight drawn positions of a close-grip EZ-bar press, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Start with the EZ-bar over the chest, elbows tucked.
Lower to the chest with the elbows close to the ribs.
Keep the elbows tucked as the bar descends.
Bar at the chest; keep the shoulder blades set.
Pause at the chest.
Press through the same line.
Keep pressing with the elbows tucked.
Finish over the chest with straight arms.

entries.name: Dumbbell Bench Press with Neutral Grip
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: on the flat bench, the two bells stand VERTICAL above the grip so the palms-facing-each-other orientation is drawn visibly, and the elbows lower out to the side to the torso. No database media row exists under this name; the standard neutral-grip setup was drawn (listed in the daily review). Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Eight drawn positions of a dumbbell bench press with a neutral grip, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Start with the bells above you, palms facing each other.
Lower with the elbows out to the side.
Keep the palms facing each other as the bells descend.
Bells at the torso; keep the shoulder blades set.
Pause at the bottom of the rep.
Extend the elbows back to the start.
Keep the palms facing each other.
Finish with the arms straight above you.

entries.name: Extended Range One-Arm Kettlebell Floor Press
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, from the description accepted that day: the earlier drawing showed a flat floor press, with no roll of the body and no knee taken across. Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 12 degrees and seen from a little above, so the roll and the arm out on the floor show: lying on the floor with the near knee bent and its foot planted across the body, the hips and trunk rolled away from the pressing arm so that shoulder is off the floor, and the free arm out on the floor; the kettlebell starts beside the shoulder with the elbow sunk below the line of the chest and is pressed to a straight upright arm, a short pause, and a slower lowering. The body and legs do not move. One side is shown; the last caption carries the change of sides. The roll is drawn already taken; rolling into it is in the first caption only.
entries.summary: Lying on the floor with one knee taken across so the trunk rolls away from the kettlebell, press it to a straight vertical arm, lower under control only as far as the shoulder is comfortable, then change sides.

frames.caption: Lie on your back holding a kettlebell by the handle at one shoulder, then bend that side's leg and take the knee across your body so the hips and trunk roll toward the other side and the pressing shoulder lifts off the floor, with the free arm out on the floor for support.
Press the kettlebell up until the arm is straight and vertical, drawing the upper arm in toward the chest as it rises.
Knee across, trunk rolled away from the kettlebell.
Lower under control, letting the elbow sink behind the line of the chest only as far as the shoulder is comfortable.
Complete the repetitions, then change sides.

entries.name: One Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: on the flat bench one arm works the press line while the free arm rests still beside the torso and only the working hand carries a bell. Standard one-side setup chosen from the template; listed in the daily review. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Eight drawn positions of a one arm dumbbell bench press, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Start with the dumbbell above the chest, one arm working.
Lower with the elbow out to the side.
Keep lowering toward the chest.
Dumbbell at the chest; the free arm stays put.
Pause at the bottom.
Press back through the same line.
Keep pressing to the start.
Finish with a straight arm.

entries.name: JM Press
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: on the flat bench the bar finishes high over the upper chest with the elbows kept at the torso line - the JM press read - and the bar is drawn end-on with its plates from the b joint. No database media row exists under this name; the standard setup was drawn (listed in the daily review). Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Eight drawn positions of a JM press, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Start with the bar over the chest and the elbows tucked.
Lower with the elbows staying close to the body.
Keep the bar path tight as it descends.
Bar touches high; elbows stay under the bar.
Pause without losing the tuck.
Press back through the same short line.
Keep the elbows leading the press.
Finish over the chest with straight arms.

frames.caption: Lie on the bench with the feet planted and both dumbbells settled over the chest.
Lower the bells beside the chest with the wrists stacked over the elbows.
Keep each wrist stacked over its elbow and the upper back anchored.
Press both bells along the same path so the sides stay matched.
Hold the top with the wrists stacked and the upper back anchored.

entries.summary: Five drawn positions of a dumbbell bench press, seen from the side.

entries.name: Competition Bench
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 28 degrees: feet planted on the floor, upper back and hips pinned to the flat bench throughout, unracking to straight arms, lowering to the lower-chest touch point with vertical stacked forearms, holding a 900 ms competition pause on the chest, and pressing back to lockout.
entries.summary: Plant the feet and pin the upper back to the bench, take a competition-width grip and unrack to straight arms, lower to the lower-chest touch point with stacked forearms, hold the competition pause, and press back to lockout.

frames.caption: Plant the feet and pin the upper back to the bench before taking a secure competition-width grip, then unrack to straight arms and settle the bar.
Lower to the same lower-chest touch point with stacked forearms.
Hold the competition pause on the chest with the feet planted and hips and upper back pinned to the bench.
Press back to lockout.
Drive the feet and pin the upper back, touch the same lower-chest point, hold the pause, then press.

entries.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 28 degrees: hands set at shoulder width rather than touching or competition-wide, elbows riding close to the ribs as the bar lowers to the lower chest with vertical forearms, and pressing back up to straight arms.
entries.summary: Lie on a bench with a shoulder-width grip, unrack to straight arms, lower the bar to the lower chest with the elbows staying close to the sides, and press back up to straight arms.

frames.caption: Lie on a bench and grip the bar at about shoulder width, not narrower, then unrack to straight arms.
Lower the bar to your lower chest with your elbows staying close to your sides and wrists stacked over the elbows.
Touch low on the chest with the elbows riding close to the ribs and forearms vertical.
Press back up to straight arms.
Elbows ride close to the ribs, wrists stacked over the elbows, touch low on the chest, and press to straight arms.

entries.name: Decline Bench Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 28 degrees: a head-lower decline bench, legs hooked under the rollers, a just-wider-than-shoulder grip, a short stroke to the lower chest with vertical forearms, and lockout over the eyes.
entries.summary: With your legs hooked into a decline bench and a grip just wider than shoulder width, lower to the lower line of your chest with stacked forearms and press back to lockout over your eyes.

frames.caption: Hook your legs into the decline bench, take the bar just wider than shoulder width, and have a spotter for the unrack to lockout over your eyes.
Lower to the lower line of your chest with the wrists stacked and bar over the forearm bones.
Touch at the natural end of the shorter decline stroke at the lower chest.
Press back to lockout over your eyes.
Hook your legs into the decline bench, touch at the natural end of the shorter stroke with stacked wrists, and press back to lockout over your eyes.

entries.name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 28 degrees: legs secured in the decline bench rollers with the torso on the head-lower pad, lowering two independent dumbbells to the sides of the lower chest with vertical forearms, and pressing up and slightly inward to the top.
entries.summary: With the legs secured in a decline bench and the shoulder blades pinned into the pad, lower the dumbbells toward the lower chest with vertical forearms, then press up and slightly inward.

frames.caption: Secure the legs in a decline bench, sit with the dumbbells on the thighs, then lie back and bring the bells to the chest before pressing them into position.
Lower toward the lower chest with the forearms vertical and the shoulder blades pinned into the pad.
Reach the bottom at the sides of the lower chest with the wrists stacked over the elbows.
Press up and slightly inward to the top.
Pin the shoulder blades into the pad, stack the wrists over the elbows, and press up and slightly inward.

entries.name: Board Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 28 degrees: lowering the barbell under control until it settles on the surface of the chest-banded boards in a shortened range of motion, then driving up with force to lockout.
entries.summary: With boards banded securely to the chest, feet set, and back arched on the bench, lower the bar under control until it settles on the boards, then drive the bar up with the elbows tucked to lockout.

frames.caption: Lie on the bench with the boards banded securely to the chest, set the feet, arch the back, retract the shoulder blades, and unrack to lockout.
Lower the bar under control with the elbows tucked toward the boards.
Let the bar settle on the boards banded to the chest.
Drive the bar up with force, keeping the elbows tucked until lockout.
Keep the boards banded and fixed to the chest, let the bar settle on the boards, and keep the elbows tucked to lockout.

entries.name: Pin Presses
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 28 degrees: starting from a dead stop on the rack pins, driving the bar up to straight arms with bar, wrists, and elbows aligned, and lowering back to settle on the pins for a full pause.
entries.summary: Lying on a bench inside a rack with the bar resting on pins above your usual touch point, drive the bar from a full pause up to straight arms, then lower it back to the pins and let it settle.

frames.caption: Set a bench inside a rack with the pins at the chosen height above your usual touch point and the bar resting on them, shoulder blades pulled together and feet set.
From a full pause on the pins, drive the bar up to straight arms, keeping the bar, wrists and elbows in line.
Reach straight arms at the top with the bar, wrists and elbows in line.
Lower the bar back to the pins and let it settle before the next repetition.
Shoulder blades pulled together, drive from a full pause on the pins, and settle the bar on the pins each time.

entries.name: Floor Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 28 degrees: lying directly on the floor with the head inside a rack with low hooks and knees bent with feet flat, holding the barbell with straight arms, lowering with tucked elbows until the upper arms rest flat on the floor for a full pause, and pressing back up to straight arms.
entries.summary: Lie on the floor with your head inside a rack and lift the bar off low hooks with straight arms, lower toward the lower chest until the upper arms rest on the floor and pause, then press back up.

frames.caption: Lie on the floor with your head inside a rack, the bar set on low hooks, shoulder blades pulled together, and lift the bar off with straight arms.
Lower the bar toward the lower chest with the elbows tucked until the upper arms rest on the floor.
Pause with the upper arms resting on the floor and the wrists stacked over the elbows.
Press the bar back up, keeping the bar, wrists and elbows in line.
Shoulder blades pulled together, pause with the upper arms on the floor, and keep the wrists stacked over the elbows.

entries.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Floor Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 45 degrees the other way: the single kettlebell in the working near hand, the palm-in bottom with the upper arm resting on the floor 45 degrees out from the trunk and the wrist stacked over the elbow, the bell rising from over the elbow to over the shoulder as the wrist turns until the arm is straight and vertical, and the slower 1450 ms lowering phase.
entries.summary: Lying on the floor with one upper arm resting on the ground and the palm facing in holding a kettlebell, press the kettlebell straight up while letting the wrist turn, then lower it slowly until the upper arm rests on the floor again.

frames.caption: Lie on the floor holding a kettlebell in one hand with that upper arm resting on the floor and the palm facing inward.
Press the kettlebell straight up until the arm is straight, letting the wrist turn as it rises.
The arm is straight and the wrist has turned.
Lower the kettlebell slowly until the upper arm rests on the floor again.
Wrist stacked over the elbow, press straight up, lower until the arm rests on the floor, and change arms after the repetitions.
